recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reapply the literal 2017 Jira XML because later applied decisions intentionally refactored the terminology source, binding strength, metadata, and canonical name while preserving FHIR-11070's substantive correction.
issue_request: FHIR-11070 was a Published DSTU2 CBCC change request resolved Not Persuasive with Modification. It asked to replace the poor original Consent.category example value set with a richer sample Consent Directive Type value set drawing on established consent-related terminologies instead of ad hoc cat1-cat6 examples.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in git-svn commit 6c5132df04 (svn revision 11255), which changed source/consent/valueset-consent-category.xml and source/consent/codesystem-consent-category.xml for Consent.category.
additional_context: Consent is active in the current build. Later Consent-category decisions changed the same artifact family: FHIR-15115 moved toward extensible vocabularies, FHIR-31904 later made Consent.category 0..* with an example binding, FHIR-44625 removed LOINC display values, FHIR-48780 promoted Consent terminology metadata, and 2025 maintenance renamed the value set to consent-category-example and fixed its canonical URL. Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct FHIR-11070 discussion that would alter this conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active Consent.category definition binds at example strength to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/consent-category-example, and the current value set includes THO/v2/v3/LOINC consent directive type sources without reintroducing the poor ad hoc category set targeted by the issue.
